entries.text: I cannot guarantee an outcome from a prepared reply. A review needs the work itself and the criteria it will be judged against.

entries.title: Make room for imperfect work
entries.prompt: I worry that taking longer means I am bad at this.
entries.text: Time can reflect many things, including the task and your circumstances. Choose a useful next step without turning the clock into a judgement.

entries.title: Make life admin manageable
entries.prompt: I am avoiding opening my post.
entries.text: Choose one envelope and a place to put it. You only need to find out what that one item needs next.

entries.title: Make life admin manageable
entries.prompt: I have forms to fill in and feel overwhelmed.
entries.text: Read just the first section and gather what it asks for. Complete one part before looking at the whole form again.

entries.title: Make life admin manageable
entries.prompt: I keep forgetting to book an appointment.
entries.text: Write down the booking details and choose a time to contact them. Verify any reminder you create.

entries.title: Make life admin manageable
entries.prompt: Can you book my medical appointment?
entries.text: Daywell cannot make that booking through a saved audio reply. Contact your provider through its booking system.

entries.title: Make life admin manageable
entries.prompt: I have a pile of small admin jobs.
entries.text: Pick one with a real deadline. Put the others in one visible list so they do not all need to stay in your head.

entries.title: Make life admin manageable
entries.prompt: I am scared to check an overdue bill.
entries.text: Open the information when you feel able, and note the actual amount and deadline. For debt advice, use a qualified support service.

entries.title: Make life admin manageable
entries.prompt: I need to organise documents for tomorrow.
entries.text: List only what tomorrow requires. Gather those items into one place and check the essentials before adding anything extra.

entries.title: Make life admin manageable
entries.prompt: Can you send that email for me?
entries.text: Sending an email needs the message, recipient, and an actual sending tool. This recording cannot send it.

entries.title: Make life admin manageable
entries.prompt: I forgot a deadline and feel ashamed.
entries.text: Find out what action is still possible now. A practical message or next step may help more than replaying the mistake.

entries.title: Make life admin manageable
entries.prompt: I want to stop putting every small job off.
entries.text: Choose one manageable job for today and make its first step obvious. You do not need to fix the whole backlog at once.

entries.title: A gentler study session
entries.prompt: I keep reading the same paragraph.
entries.text: Pause and ask what the paragraph is trying to say. Write one rough sentence in your own words, then check it against the text.

entries.title: A gentler study session
entries.prompt: I do not know how to start revising.
entries.text: Choose one topic and one small question about it. Start by seeing what you can recall before checking your notes.

entries.title: A gentler study session
entries.prompt: I have an exam tomorrow and feel behind.
entries.text: Choose the most useful topics for the time left, and leave room for ordinary needs and sleep. Avoid trying to cover everything perfectly.

entries.title: A gentler study session
entries.prompt: Studying feels lonely.
entries.text: A quiet study group or a trusted person working nearby may help. You can also use a short timer to give the session a shape.

entries.title: A gentler study session
entries.prompt: I have too many study resources open.
entries.text: Pick one resource for the next question. Keep the others available for a specific gap instead of moving between all of them.

entries.title: A gentler study session
entries.prompt: Can you explain this topic to me?
entries.text: Tell me the topic and the part that is confusing. A useful explanation needs that context rather than a generic recording.

entries.title: A gentler study session
entries.prompt: I am tired but have more to study.
entries.text: Check whether a break or stopping for the day would be more useful. More time at the desk is not always more learning.

entries.title: A gentler study session
entries.prompt: I cannot remember anything I studied.
entries.text: Try one small recall question and then check your notes. Begin with a narrow topic rather than testing yourself on everything.

entries.title: A gentler study session
entries.prompt: I want to end studying with a clear next step.
entries.text: Write the next topic and one question to start with. That gives your next session a place to begin.

entries.title: A gentler study session
entries.prompt: Can you do my exam for me?
entries.text: I can support practice and understanding, but I cannot take an exam on your behalf. We can work on the topic you need to learn.

entries.title: Look back without a score
entries.prompt: How has my week been?
entries.text: Your saved history can help you look back. Choose one thing that supported you and one thing you would like to make easier.

entries.title: Look back without a score
entries.prompt: I want to review today without judging myself.
entries.text: Describe what happened before deciding what it means. Include your circumstances, your effort, and any support you had.

entries.title: Look back without a score
entries.prompt: What went well for me today?
entries.text: Think of one moment that felt useful, kind, or manageable. It can be ordinary and still belong in your reflection.

entries.title: Look back without a score
entries.prompt: Can you summarise my month?
entries.text: A monthly summary needs your actual saved entries. Open your history and choose the period you want to review.

entries.title: Look back without a score
entries.prompt: I cannot remember what I achieved this week.
entries.text: Look for small records: an appointment attended, a meal made, a walk, or a moment of rest. Progress can be quiet.

entries.title: Look back without a score
entries.prompt: I want a question to reflect on tonight.
entries.text: Try this: what made today a little easier, and would I like to make room for it again?

entries.title: Look back without a score
entries.prompt: My week was difficult; can I still record it?
entries.text: Yes. Your history can include difficult days without needing a positive ending. A plain note is enough.

entries.title: Look back without a score
entries.prompt: I only remember the things I did not finish.
entries.text: Take a second look at what you did carry through, including ordinary care and responsibilities that may be easy to overlook.

entries.title: Look back without a score
entries.prompt: Can we do a very short weekly check in?
entries.text: Name one helpful thing, one difficult thing, and one small adjustment for next week. You can stop after those three.

entries.title: Look back without a score
entries.prompt: I want to remember how this part of my life felt.
entries.text: Write a few words about the day as it was. Your record can hold experience as well as completed tasks.

entries.title: Return after a gap
entries.prompt: I have not used Daywell for two weeks.
entries.text: You can start with today. There is no backlog of app visits you need to catch up on.

entries.title: Return after a gap
entries.prompt: My history has lots of empty days.
entries.text: Empty spaces mean there is no entry, not that nothing happened. You can leave those spaces as they are.

entries.title: Return after a gap
entries.prompt: I broke my routine and feel like starting over is pointless.
entries.text: The earlier effort still happened. Choose a version of the routine that fits where you are now.

entries.title: Return after a gap
entries.prompt: Do I need to fill in every missing day?
entries.text: Only if it is useful to you. A record can be helpful without being complete.

entries.title: Return after a gap
entries.prompt: I am embarrassed to come back after disappearing.
entries.text: There is no explanation you owe the app. Choose one thing that would help you today.

entries.title: Return after a gap
entries.prompt: Can you hide the days when I did nothing?
entries.text: An empty day does not prove you did nothing. Review the available history controls if you want to change how entries are shown.

entries.title: Return after a gap
entries.prompt: I forgot my habit again.
entries.text: Look at what got in the way this time. A smaller step or a different cue may fit better than a stronger promise.

entries.title: Return after a gap
entries.prompt: I used to do this regularly and now I do not.
entries.text: Your circumstances may have changed. Begin with what is manageable now rather than demanding the old routine immediately.

entries.title: Return after a gap
entries.prompt: Can a restart count as progress?
entries.text: A return can be useful in itself. You noticed a need and chose to respond to it again.

entries.title: Return after a gap
entries.prompt: I want a fresh start without deleting my past.
entries.text: You can choose a new intention for today while keeping your earlier records. The past can stay without directing every next step.

entries.title: Notice an ordinary win
entries.prompt: I finally did the small task I was avoiding.
entries.text: Give that moment a little room. You took a step that had been difficult to begin.

entries.title: Notice an ordinary win
entries.prompt: All I managed was getting dressed.
entries.text: That was part of caring for yourself today. You can acknowledge it without comparing it with someone else's day.

entries.title: Notice an ordinary win
entries.prompt: I took a break before I got completely overwhelmed.
entries.text: You noticed what you needed and responded. That is a useful moment to remember.

entries.title: Notice an ordinary win
entries.prompt: I went for a short walk instead of scrolling.
entries.text: You made space for something different. Notice what the walk was like, without needing it to become a bigger achievement.

entries.title: Notice an ordinary win
entries.prompt: I cooked once this week.
entries.text: You made one meal happen. If it helped, note what made it manageable so you can return to it.

entries.title: Notice an ordinary win
entries.prompt: I asked for help and that was hard.
entries.text: Asking for support can take effort. You do not have to manage every difficulty on your own.

entries.title: Notice an ordinary win
entries.prompt: I stopped working at a reasonable time.
entries.text: You made an ending to the workday. Let the time you protected be available for what you need now.

entries.title: Notice an ordinary win
entries.prompt: I chose rest instead of forcing another workout.
entries.text: You paid attention to your circumstances. Recovery and rest can belong alongside movement.

entries.title: Notice an ordinary win
entries.prompt: Can you save this as a win?
entries.text: Add a note to your history or journal and check it saved. The recording itself cannot create that entry.

entries.title: Notice an ordinary win
entries.prompt: I do not want a big celebration, just a little acknowledgement.
entries.text: A quiet acknowledgement is enough: that took some effort, and you did it. Nothing more needs to be made of it.

entries.title: Get curious about patterns
entries.prompt: I always struggle on Mondays.
entries.text: Look at what Mondays ask of you. A smaller plan or a little preparation may help more than blaming yourself.

entries.title: Get curious about patterns
entries.prompt: My energy seems different every day.
entries.text: A brief note about the day may help you notice patterns over time. Avoid treating one entry as the whole explanation.

entries.title: Get curious about patterns
entries.prompt: I feel better on days I leave the house.
entries.text: That is worth noticing. Think about what part of going out helps and whether a manageable version fits another day.

entries.title: Get curious about patterns
entries.prompt: I scroll most when I am exhausted.
entries.text: The scrolling may be filling a need for a low effort pause. Try keeping another easy resting option available.

entries.title: Get curious about patterns
entries.prompt: I only exercise when a friend comes with me.
entries.text: Company may be a useful support. You can plan with that in mind instead of treating it as a weakness.

entries.title: Get curious about patterns
entries.prompt: I notice I miss meals when meetings run late.
entries.text: That gives you a practical place to adjust. Could you protect a food break or keep an accessible backup option?

entries.title: Get curious about patterns
entries.prompt: I want to compare two weeks without competing with myself.
entries.text: Look for differences in circumstances as well as activities. Ask what helped, rather than which week deserves a higher score.

entries.title: Get curious about patterns
entries.prompt: Everything seems linked and I cannot find one cause.
entries.text: You do not need one perfect explanation. Choose a small change you can observe, and seek professional help for persistent health concerns.

entries.title: Make space in the calendar
entries.prompt: What is on my calendar tomorrow?
entries.text: Open tomorrow in your calendar to see the saved plans. A prerecorded reply cannot read your current schedule.

entries.title: Make space in the calendar
entries.prompt: Add a walk to my calendar on Friday.
entries.text: Choose Friday and add the walk with the time you want. Check the saved date so it appears where you expect.

entries.title: Make space in the calendar
entries.prompt: Move my workout to next week.
entries.text: Open the scheduled workout and choose its new date. Review the change before saving it.

entries.title: Make space in the calendar
entries.prompt: I have planned too much for tomorrow.
entries.text: Choose what genuinely needs to happen, then move or remove something that can wait. Leave space between commitments.

entries.title: Make space in the calendar
entries.prompt: Can you schedule time to do nothing?
entries.text: You can add a rest block to your calendar. Give it enough room to feel like a pause, rather than another performance.

entries.title: Make space in the calendar
entries.prompt: Show me my next free evening.
entries.text: That requires your actual calendar entries. Review the coming evenings and include commitments that may not be recorded.

entries.title: Make space in the calendar
entries.prompt: Can you remind me of my appointment next month?
entries.text: Create and verify a reminder in a calendar or alarm service that supports notifications. A saved Daywell plan alone may not notify you.

entries.title: Make space in the calendar
entries.prompt: I want travel time around my appointment.
entries.text: Add a little preparation and journey time around the appointment. A calendar is more useful when it includes getting there.

entries.title: Make space in the calendar
entries.prompt: Delete tomorrow's planned run.
entries.text: Find the planned run on tomorrow's date and confirm it is the right entry before removing it.

entries.title: Make space in the calendar
entries.prompt: Can I plan a gentle week instead of a productive one?
entries.text: Yes. Leave space for sleep, meals, movement you want, and rest. Your calendar can reflect care as well as commitments.

entries.title: See how far you have come
entries.prompt: Show me the days I moved this month.
entries.text: Open your history for the month and review the movement entries. Remember that unlogged activity will not appear there.

entries.title: See how far you have come
entries.prompt: When did I last take a proper rest day?
entries.text: That needs your saved history and what rest means to you. Look back for a day with room to recover.

entries.title: See how far you have come
entries.prompt: Can I add something I did yesterday?
entries.text: You can make a dated entry for yesterday where the app supports it. Check the date before saving.

entries.title: See how far you have come
entries.prompt: I want to remember my first workout here.
entries.text: Look for the earliest movement entry in your history. You can add a reflection about what that beginning meant to you.

entries.title: See how far you have come
entries.prompt: I cannot see an activity I remember doing.
entries.text: It may not have been logged, or it may be under another date. Check the records before assuming it was lost.

entries.title: See how far you have come
entries.prompt: Does an empty calendar day mean I failed?
entries.text: No. A calendar shows recorded plans and entries. It cannot measure your effort or everything that mattered that day.

entries.title: See how far you have come
entries.prompt: I want to compare where I started with now.
entries.text: Choose one meaningful change, such as an easier routine or asking for help sooner. Progress does not have to be a number.

entries.title: See how far you have come
entries.prompt: Can you mark a past task as completed?
entries.text: Open the correct task and update its status. Check the date and details so your history remains accurate.

entries.title: See how far you have come
entries.prompt: I need to correct yesterday's activity record.
entries.text: Find the entry in your history and edit the details available there. Review it after saving to confirm the correction.

entries.title: See how far you have come
entries.prompt: My calendar only shows tasks; I want memories too.
entries.text: A short journal note can capture the experience around a day. Useful history can include how things felt, not only what got done.

entries.title: Keep your plans connected
entries.prompt: Can you connect directly to Google Calendar?
entries.text: Daywell currently offers calendar file export, rather than live Google Calendar synchronisation. Check the export options in the calendar.

entries.title: Keep your plans connected
entries.prompt: Can I put Daywell plans in Apple Calendar?
entries.text: You can use the calendar export file with a compatible calendar app. Check the imported dates and times after adding it.

entries.title: Keep your plans connected
entries.prompt: Will my Apple Calendar changes update Daywell automatically?
entries.text: A calendar file export is a snapshot. Changes in another calendar do not automatically update Daywell.

entries.title: Keep your plans connected
entries.prompt: Export my upcoming plans.
entries.text: Use the calendar export control, then check the dates included in the file before importing it elsewhere.

entries.title: Keep your plans connected
entries.prompt: I imported the same calendar file twice.
entries.text: The receiving calendar may contain duplicates. Review those entries there before removing anything you want to keep.

entries.title: Keep your plans connected
entries.prompt: Can you see all my Google events now?
entries.text: A prepared reply cannot access your Google events. Daywell's file export does not grant access to that calendar.

entries.title: Keep your plans connected
entries.prompt: My event has the wrong time after importing.
entries.text: Check the time zone and event details in both places. Correct the event only after confirming which time you intended.

entries.title: Keep your plans connected
entries.prompt: Can I share a calendar export with someone?
entries.text: An export can contain personal plans. Review its contents and share it only with someone you intend to receive those details.

entries.title: Keep your plans connected
entries.prompt: Can Daywell keep a history without an external calendar?
entries.text: You can use Daywell's own calendar and history. Connecting another calendar is not required to keep a record.

entries.title: Keep your plans connected
entries.prompt: I want one source of truth for my schedule.
entries.text: Choose which calendar you will check regularly. With file exports, review changes carefully because the copies do not stay in sync.

entries.title: Prepare for a commitment
entries.prompt: I have an appointment and feel scattered.
entries.text: Check the time, place, and what you need to bring. Keep those details in one place you can find easily.

entries.title: Prepare for a commitment
entries.prompt: What should I ask at my next health appointment?
entries.text: Write down your main concern, how long it has been happening, and any questions you do not want to forget.

entries.title: Prepare for a commitment
entries.prompt: Can you add my appointment details for me?
entries.text: The calendar needs the date, time, and details you want saved. Review the entry before confirming it.

entries.title: Prepare for a commitment
entries.prompt: I keep leaving too late for appointments.
entries.text: Work backwards from arrival time and include getting ready. A separate leaving reminder may be more useful than the appointment time alone.

entries.title: Prepare for a commitment
entries.prompt: I am worried I will forget what the clinician said.
entries.text: You can take notes and ask for clarification or written instructions. Bring a trusted person if that is appropriate and you want support.

entries.title: Prepare for a commitment
entries.prompt: I need to reschedule something I cannot manage.
entries.text: Check how to contact the organiser and ask about the next available option. Update your calendar once the new time is confirmed.

entries.title: Prepare for a commitment
entries.prompt: I want a little recovery time after a difficult meeting.
entries.text: Leave a small gap after it if you can. A short pause can give you room before the next commitment.

entries.title: Prepare for a commitment
entries.prompt: I missed an appointment and do not know what to do.
entries.text: Contact the provider or organiser to find out the next step. Then update your plans with the confirmed information.

entries.title: Prepare for a commitment
entries.prompt: Can you remind me what I wanted to discuss?
entries.text: That needs your saved notes. Open the relevant entry and check the questions you recorded.

entries.title: Put a setback in context
entries.prompt: I feel worse this week than last week.
entries.text: A difficult week does not erase earlier helpful moments. Consider what changed, and seek support if you are struggling to cope.

entries.title: Put a setback in context
entries.prompt: My progress has gone backwards.
entries.text: Look at the circumstances around the change. You may need a different amount of support or a smaller plan right now.

entries.title: Put a setback in context
entries.prompt: I had one good week and then everything fell apart.
entries.text: One difficult period does not make the good week unreal. Keep the useful parts and adjust what no longer fits.

entries.title: Put a setback in context
entries.prompt: I am disappointed with my record.
entries.text: A record is information, not a grade. Ask what would make the next few days more manageable.

entries.title: Put a setback in context
entries.prompt: Other people improve faster than I do.
entries.text: Their circumstances and starting points may be different. Choose a change that is meaningful in your own life.

entries.title: Put a setback in context
entries.prompt: I want to delete my history because it makes me feel bad.
entries.text: You can pause reviewing it and think about what information is useful to keep. Check what deletion removes before making that choice.

entries.title: Put a setback in context
entries.prompt: I expected this app to fix everything quickly.
entries.text: An app can offer tools and small supports, but change can take time and outside help. You do not have to do it all here.

entries.title: Put a setback in context
entries.prompt: I am doing the habits but still struggling.
entries.text: Habits are not a substitute for the support you may need. Consider speaking with a qualified professional or someone you trust.

entries.title: Put a setback in context
entries.prompt: Can we choose a smaller goal after this setback?
entries.text: Choose something that fits the next day, not your most ambitious week. A manageable step can give you a place to return.

entries.title: Care for the longer term
entries.prompt: Can Daywell make me live longer?
entries.text: Daywell cannot promise a longer life. It can support everyday routines around movement, food, rest, and sleep.

entries.title: Care for the longer term
entries.prompt: I want to feel stronger as I get older.
entries.text: A manageable movement routine may support that aim. Get appropriate guidance for your health and abilities as you build it.

entries.title: Care for the longer term
entries.prompt: I want habits I can keep for years.
entries.text: Choose a version that fits ordinary, busy weeks. A flexible routine is easier to return to when life changes.

entries.title: Care for the longer term
entries.prompt: Should I optimise every part of my life?
entries.text: You do not need to turn life into constant measurement. Choose a few supports that leave room for enjoyment and rest.

entries.title: Care for the longer term
entries.prompt: I want health progress without chasing a perfect score.
entries.text: Focus on activities and routines that matter to you. A score cannot capture your whole health or your life.

entries.title: Care for the longer term
entries.prompt: What is one long term intention I could set?
entries.text: Try an intention about how you want daily life to feel, such as having more room for rest or easier access to movement.

entries.title: Care for the longer term
entries.prompt: I want to take care of myself without making it another job.
entries.text: Let the routine remove friction. Choose fewer steps and make room for days when only the basics happen.

entries.title: Care for the longer term
entries.prompt: How will I know whether this app is helping?
entries.text: Notice whether it makes useful actions easier or gives you a welcome pause. You can keep what helps and drop what does not.

entries.title: Care for the longer term
entries.prompt: Can I change what progress means to me?
entries.text: Yes. Your priorities can change with your circumstances. Choose a definition that supports the life you are living now.

entries.title: An easy way to begin
entries.prompt: Hello, Daywell.
entries.text: Hello. You can arrive just as you are. What would make this moment a little easier?

entries.title: An easy way to begin
entries.prompt: I am back after a very busy day.
entries.text: Welcome back. You can put the day down for a moment. A quiet pause is a good enough place to start.

entries.title: An easy way to begin
entries.prompt: I do not really know why I opened the app.
entries.text: You do not need a clear reason. You can take a small pause and see what, if anything, would help.

entries.title: An easy way to begin
entries.prompt: Is there anything I have to do here?
entries.text: There is no task you have to complete. You can listen, use a tool, or simply leave when you are ready.

entries.title: An easy way to begin
entries.prompt: I just want a gentle hello.
entries.text: Hello there. Let this be one undemanding moment in the middle of your day.

entries.title: An easy way to begin
entries.prompt: I am here but I do not want to explain everything.
entries.text: You can keep the details to yourself. Choose a quiet recording if listening feels easier than talking.

entries.title: An easy way to begin
entries.prompt: What can I say to start?
entries.text: You can say what you need in ordinary words, such as help me unwind, or I want to move a little.

entries.title: An easy way to begin
entries.prompt: I am trying this for the first time.
entries.text: Start with one small need. You can explore a guided moment or a simple tool without setting up your whole life.

entries.title: An easy way to begin
entries.prompt: Can I use this without having a goal?
entries.text: Yes. A few quiet minutes can be a complete visit. You do not need to turn them into a goal.

entries.title: An easy way to begin
entries.prompt: I am having a very ordinary day.
entries.text: Ordinary days belong here too. You can make room for a small comfort without waiting for a difficult moment.

entries.title: One host, friendly company
entries.prompt: Do I need to remember all the mascot names?
entries.text: No. You can ask Daywell in your own words. The companions are there to make the experience feel welcoming.

entries.title: One host, friendly company
entries.prompt: Who should I ask for help sleeping?
entries.text: Just ask Daywell for a gentle sleep or wind down moment. You do not need to call a separate companion.

entries.title: One host, friendly company
entries.prompt: What does Luma do?
entries.text: Luma accompanies quiet moments, rest, and settling down. You can simply choose the kind of support you want.

entries.title: One host, friendly company
entries.prompt: What does Bounce do?
entries.text: Bounce brings friendly company to movement. You can ask Daywell about moving without remembering a special command.

entries.title: One host, friendly company
entries.prompt: What does Pip help with?
entries.text: Pip accompanies focus and manageable next steps. The task can stay small, even when your thoughts feel busy.

entries.title: One host, friendly company
entries.prompt: Why are Momo and Nori here?
entries.text: They bring a little company to food and everyday care. You do not need to manage them or give them separate instructions.

entries.title: One host, friendly company
entries.prompt: Do I have to look after the mascots?
entries.text: No. The companions do not need feeding, attention, or a daily visit. They are here to support your experience.

entries.title: One host, friendly company
entries.prompt: Will a mascot be disappointed if I skip a day?
entries.text: No companion is keeping score or waiting for an explanation. You can return whenever the app is useful.

entries.title: One host, friendly company
entries.prompt: Can I just talk to one main assistant?
entries.text: That is the idea: use ordinary words with Daywell. You do not need to choose a different assistant for every need.

entries.title: One host, friendly company
entries.prompt: Are these companions real people?
entries.text: The companions are illustrated characters, and the voices are AI generated. They do not have human experiences or feelings.

entries.title: Choose how you listen
entries.prompt: Can I hear a calmer voice?
entries.text: In the new unwind sessions, choose a voice and use its preview button. The full session begins only when you press begin.

entries.title: Choose how you listen
entries.prompt: Turn the volume down.
entries.text: Use the voice volume control in the session or your device volume. This saved reply cannot change that setting.

entries.title: Choose how you listen
entries.prompt: Stop talking for a moment.
entries.text: Use the stop or pause control when you want quiet. You are free to end the audio at any time.

entries.title: Choose how you listen
entries.prompt: Can you repeat the last bit?
entries.text: Use the session position control to move back, or replay a short recording. Choose only as much as you want to hear.

entries.title: Choose how you listen
entries.prompt: Do I need headphones for meditation?
entries.text: Headphones are optional. Use a comfortable listening setup and volume, in a place where it is safe to settle.

entries.title: Choose how you listen
entries.prompt: Can I listen without speaking?
entries.text: Yes. Just listen contains prerecorded moments. Those recordings do not need microphone access.

entries.title: Choose how you listen
entries.prompt: Will you start playing when I select a voice?
entries.text: Selecting an unwind voice does not start audio. Use preview or begin when you are ready to listen.

entries.title: Choose how you listen
entries.prompt: I want to read instead of listen.
entries.text: The guidance is available as text. Open the full guidance if you would like to follow the session in writing.

entries.title: Choose how you listen
entries.prompt: Can I keep the audio playing while I drive?
entries.text: Use these settling exercises after you have arrived safely. Do not follow relaxation or breathing cues while driving.

entries.title: Choose how you listen
entries.prompt: Can you speak in another language?
entries.text: These saved recordings are in English. Other languages would need supported, separately prepared guidance or a live conversation.

entries.title: Understand what you share
entries.prompt: Is my microphone on while a recording plays?
entries.text: Prerecorded listening does not require the microphone. Check the separate live voice control if you have started a conversation.

entries.title: Understand what you share
entries.prompt: Does a live voice conversation use an outside service?
entries.text: Live voice uses ElevenLabs after you choose to connect. Review the consent and privacy information before starting.

entries.title: Understand what you share
entries.prompt: Should I say my password to Daywell?
entries.text: Keep passwords, payment details, and private security codes out of conversations. They are not needed for a calming moment.

entries.title: Understand what you share
entries.prompt: Can you delete everything you know about me?
entries.text: Data deletion needs the appropriate account or data controls. A prerecorded reply cannot delete stored information.

entries.title: Understand what you share
entries.prompt: Can other people using this device see my app?
entries.text: That depends on the device and account session. Use appropriate device protection and check your sign in state when sharing a device.

entries.title: Understand what you share
entries.prompt: Do you automatically send my journal to the voice service?
entries.text: Daywell's live voice setup does not automatically include your journal. What you choose to say in a conversation is still shared with the voice service.

entries.title: Understand what you share
entries.prompt: Can I use a vague description instead of personal details?
entries.text: Yes. You can say you had a difficult day without naming people or sharing private information.

entries.title: Understand what you share
entries.prompt: Where can I check the current privacy terms?
entries.text: Use the privacy information provided for the app and its voice service. A saved reply may not reflect later changes to those terms.

entries.title: Understand what you share
entries.prompt: Can you promise this conversation is completely confidential?
entries.text: I cannot make that promise. Check how the app and its voice provider process data before sharing sensitive information.

entries.title: Understand what you share
entries.prompt: I accidentally said something sensitive.
entries.text: End the live conversation if you want to stop sharing. Check the service's data controls or support options for any stored information.

entries.title: Make the experience comfortable
entries.prompt: The mascot movement is distracting me.
entries.text: Use the gentle movement control to turn animation off. You can keep the companion still while you listen.

entries.title: Make the experience comfortable
entries.prompt: I do not want to follow breathing instructions.
entries.text: You can leave your breathing alone. Try the room based meditation, or simply notice the support beneath you.

entries.title: Make the experience comfortable
entries.prompt: Closing my eyes makes me uncomfortable.
entries.text: Keep them open. You can rest your gaze somewhere ordinary and stay aware of the room.

entries.title: Make the experience comfortable
entries.prompt: I need fewer choices on screen.
entries.text: Choose one moment to use for now and leave the rest. You do not need to explore every option during a visit.

entries.title: Make the experience comfortable
entries.prompt: I cannot sit in the suggested position.
entries.text: Use a position that is comfortable and safe for you. You do not need to match the illustration.

entries.title: Make the experience comfortable
entries.prompt: I find breath sounds unpleasant.
entries.text: You can choose a recording without breathing demonstrations, read the guidance, or pause the audio. Your comfort matters.

entries.title: Make the experience comfortable
entries.prompt: I need a session that does not require standing.
entries.text: Choose a resting or listening session that suits your position. Adapt the setup to your comfort and access needs.

entries.title: Make the experience comfortable
entries.prompt: I do not want motivational cheering.
entries.text: A quieter approach is okay. Choose a gentle listening moment and let the next step stay small.

entries.title: Make the experience comfortable
entries.prompt: Can you make the text easier for me to read?
entries.text: Your browser or device may offer text size and zoom controls. Use the written guidance at a size that feels comfortable.

entries.title: Make the experience comfortable
entries.prompt: I want to change the look again later.
entries.text: You can return to the appearance choices when you want. A design preference does not need to become a permanent decision.

entries.title: Find the right words
entries.prompt: Help me with that thing.
entries.text: Which thing would you like help with? A few ordinary words about the situation are enough to begin.

entries.title: Find the right words
entries.prompt: Do the usual one.
entries.text: Which activity do you mean today? I do not want to choose or change something based on a guess.

entries.title: Find the right words
entries.prompt: Make it better.
entries.text: What would you like to feel a little easier right now: your next task, your body, or finding a pause?

entries.title: Find the right words
entries.prompt: I need something but cannot name it.
entries.text: Start with what you notice. Are you tired, hungry, restless, overwhelmed, or simply unsure? You can take your time.

entries.title: Find the right words
entries.prompt: Change the time.
entries.text: Which time would you like to change, and what should it be instead? The right entry needs to be clear before it is edited.

entries.title: Find the right words
entries.prompt: Remind me later.
entries.text: What should the reminder say, and when would later be useful? Check the reminder tool can deliver the notification you need.

entries.title: Find the right words
entries.prompt: Play that voice again.
entries.text: Choose the voice you mean in the unwind session, then use preview or begin. A saved recording cannot identify your previous choice.

entries.title: Find the right words
entries.prompt: I do not know whether I need rest or movement.
entries.text: Notice your energy and any discomfort. You could begin with a short pause, then decide whether gentle movement appeals.

entries.title: Find the right words
entries.prompt: Never mind, that was not what I meant.
entries.text: We can leave that idea there. Tell me what you meant in another way, without needing the perfect wording.

entries.title: Find the right words
entries.prompt: I said sleep, not a workout.
entries.text: Thanks for correcting that. Choose a sleep or wind down moment so the support fits what you actually wanted.

entries.title: When several things need attention
entries.prompt: I need dinner, a workout, and an early night.
entries.text: Choose what needs attention first, and keep the evening realistic. You can make each part smaller or leave one for another day.

entries.title: When several things need attention
entries.prompt: I am tired and hungry and still have work to do.
entries.text: Take care of an immediate ordinary need first if you can. Then reassess how much work reasonably fits the energy left.

entries.title: When several things need attention
entries.prompt: Can you plan my whole evening for me?
entries.text: Tell me your fixed commitments and the time you have. A useful plan needs those details, with some room left open.

entries.title: When several things need attention
entries.prompt: I want to calm down and then focus.
entries.text: Begin with a brief settling pause. When you are ready, choose one small task instead of the whole list.

entries.title: When several things need attention
entries.prompt: I want to exercise but also really need rest.
entries.text: You can choose rest, or a very gentle amount of movement if it suits you. The decision does not need to prove anything.

entries.title: When several things need attention
entries.prompt: I need to stop scrolling and go to bed.
entries.text: Choose one ending for the scrolling, such as closing the feed. Then take the first small step of getting ready for bed.

entries.title: When several things need attention
entries.prompt: Set a timer and add food to my shopping list.
entries.text: Those are two separate app actions. Check the timer is running, then add the food items and verify the list.

entries.title: When several things need attention
entries.prompt: I have so many habits to improve that I do nothing.
entries.text: Choose one area for now. Making one ordinary action easier can be enough to begin.

entries.title: When several things need attention
entries.prompt: Can I combine a rest break with a calendar check?
entries.text: You can, but it may be easier to let the rest break be a pause first. Check the calendar afterwards if you still want to.

entries.title: When several things need attention
entries.prompt: I want the app to decide everything for me.
entries.text: I can help narrow choices, but your preferences and circumstances still matter. Let's begin with just the next decision.

entries.title: Fit the day you actually have
entries.prompt: I got home after a long train journey.
entries.text: Let arriving have a little space. Put your things down somewhere safe and settle before asking anything else of yourself.

entries.title: Fit the day you actually have
entries.prompt: My house is busy and I cannot find quiet.
entries.text: You do not need complete silence. Find the most comfortable spot available and let the surrounding sounds be part of the moment.

entries.title: Fit the day you actually have
entries.prompt: I have children and cannot take a long break.
entries.text: Use a brief pause when it is safe and practical. Even a small moment of support can fit inside a demanding day.

entries.title: Fit the day you actually have
entries.prompt: I work shifts, so normal routines do not fit.
entries.text: Build around your own work and rest periods. The clock on someone else's routine does not have to define yours.

entries.title: Fit the day you actually have
entries.prompt: I am staying away from home this week.
entries.text: Choose one familiar comfort you can bring into the new place. The rest of the routine can be simpler for now.

entries.title: Fit the day you actually have
entries.prompt: I have very little energy today.
entries.text: Make the next step smaller and include rest where you can. You do not need to use your best day as today's standard.

entries.title: Fit the day you actually have
entries.prompt: I am caring for someone and forgetting my own needs.
entries.text: Your needs still belong in the day. Consider one practical support you could ask for, alongside a small pause for yourself.

entries.title: Fit the day you actually have
entries.prompt: My day changed unexpectedly.
entries.text: Pause and look at what is still necessary. You can make a new, smaller plan without treating the old one as a failure.

entries.title: Fit the day you actually have
entries.prompt: I do not have a cosy room like the app.
entries.text: You do not need a special room. A supported seat, a familiar object, or a small comfortable corner can be enough.

entries.title: Fit the day you actually have
entries.prompt: I just want to sit here after getting home.
entries.text: Then sitting here can be the whole plan. Let yourself arrive without turning the pause into another task.

entries.title: Leave when you are ready
entries.prompt: That is enough for today, thank you.
entries.text: You can leave it there. Take whatever was useful into the rest of your day.

entries.title: Leave when you are ready
entries.prompt: I feel ready to put my phone down now.
entries.text: Let that be your next step. There is nothing else you need to finish in the app first.

entries.title: Leave when you are ready
entries.prompt: I do not feel any different after the session.
entries.text: That can happen. You have not done it wrong, and you can choose another kind of support or simply move on.

entries.title: Leave when you are ready
entries.prompt: I want a little silence after this.
entries.text: You can pause the audio and stay quietly. The silence does not need filling.

entries.title: Leave when you are ready
entries.prompt: Can I leave halfway through a session?
entries.text: Yes. Use end for now whenever you want. You do not need to reach the final second to make the visit worthwhile.

entries.title: Leave when you are ready
entries.prompt: I am going to make myself some food now.
entries.text: That sounds like a practical next step. Let the app wait while you take care of what you need.

entries.title: Leave when you are ready
entries.prompt: I want to come back to this exercise later.
entries.text: You can find the session again in Just listen. There is no need to complete another session before returning to it.

entries.title: Leave when you are ready
entries.prompt: Can you end my live voice conversation?
entries.text: Use the end conversation control to disconnect live voice. This saved reply cannot close the connection itself.

entries.title: Leave when you are ready
entries.prompt: I do not want a reminder to return.
entries.text: You can visit when you choose. Review any reminders you have set if you no longer want them.

entries.title: Leave when you are ready
entries.prompt: Goodnight, Daywell.
entries.text: Goodnight. Let the remaining tasks wait where they can. You can settle into the rest of your evening at your own pace.
